glosses: to unpin
Enlever la goupille de sécurité d’un objet.

examples.text: Avec l'enthousiasme des désespérés, je continuerai à écrire tant qu'il me restera des mots. J'en ai des silos remplis jusqu'à la gueule et je ne me rendrai pas avant de les avoir dégoupillés jusqu'au dernier.

glosses: S’énerver de manière soudaine, éclater de colère. (à l’image d’une grenade qui, dégoupillée, explose)

examples.text: « Il va encore dégoupiller… » se dit-il en se bidonnant d’avance.

glosses: Libérer un frein, un blocage, etc.

examples.text: ... Et cette peur contamine tout le monde, d’autant qu’elle génère de la violence, puisque celle-ci est autorisée par le Coran. Si nous voulons être des hommes de paix, il faut dégoupiller ces peurs en regardant les choses en face.

glosses: To unfasten by removing a pin.

examples.text: Lady Bellaston answered with a smile, “Then you have seen this terrible man, madam; pray, is he so very fine a figure as he is represented? for Etoff entertained me last night almost two hours with him. The wench I believe is in love with him by reputation.” Here the reader will be apt to wonder; but the truth is, that Mrs Etoff, who had the honour to pin and unpin the Lady Bellaston, had received compleat information concerning the said Mr Jones, and had faithfully conveyed the same to her lady last night (or rather that morning) while she was undressing; on which accounts she had been detained in her office above the space of an hour and a half.

glosses: To detach (an icon, application, etc.) from the place where it was previously pinned.

examples.text: to unpin a program from the Taskbar

glosses: To undo the pinning or fixing of (an array in memory, a security certificate, etc.) so that it can be modified again.

examples.text: […] you can use the GCHandle class mentioned earlier to pin a heap block until you explicitly unpin it.

glosses: To get (a piece) out of a pin.
To be overcome with emotion.
To become explosively angry; to lose one's temper.

examples.text: When my dad found out I had failed the exams, he just lost it.

glosses: To be overcome with emotion.
To feel devastated, or distraught, especially when one's sadness is overwhelming.

examples.text: When she heard the news about her cousin's death, she lost it.

glosses: To be overcome with emotion.
To begin to laugh uncontrollably.

examples.text: When the teacher's chair broke, the class completely lost it.

glosses: To be overcome with emotion.
To lose one's mind, go crazy.
To cease to have a skill or ability, to lose one's touch, to be washed up.

examples.text: When you think about all she's done for the sport, it's kind of sad, but she's completely lost it over the past few years.

glosses: To lose control of a situation.

examples.text: Even then, she defended everything she had sought to achieve, saying she had “the right policies at the wrong time”. “That’s when I thought ‘she’s totally lost it’,” said a former aide.

glosses: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see lose, it.

examples.text: ‘I’m Inspector Harper, Leeds police. Where did you lose it?’ / ‘Lose it?’ He laughed. ‘I’d never lose this. It was stolen.’
